request.spec:
Show on each person their statements, one line per statement still standing (a cancelled one is
gone), oldest first, as <statement date> <due-total>. The statements a merge or a transfer brings
over show among them, by date.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their statements, one line per statement still standing (a cancelled one is
gone), oldest first, as <statement date> <due-total>. The statements a merge or a transfer brings
over show among them, by date.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person now shows their statements, one line per statement still standing, oldest first, as `<date> <due-total>`. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**The statement lines**
- **Server:** `StatementService.Summary` now holds the person's list of standing statements, so its count and last statement come from that list. `StatementView` has a new `lines` field: each statement's date (the as-of date if it has one) and due-total, sorted by date. Statements with the same date keep the order they already have, so ones brought over by a merge or a transfer fall in among the person's own by date. A cancelled statement is deleted, so it disappears from the list.
- **Front end** (`people.ts`): each person's row lists them as `person-statement-line-line` items, with `n/a` when there is no due-total. This works the same way as the snapshot lines already there. There is no audit change, since the test expects none.

**A second fix, outside the request (please review).** Scenario 2 still failed after the statement work, on a claim's due when the sheet is viewed as of a date: it showed `n/a` instead of `1.29`. The 1.29 comes from a rate on the parent sheet. That parent's today is never set, so it is the real date (2026-10-29). When the app builds the as-of view, it only took the parent's state saved on or before the as-of day (2026-03-20), so the parent came through empty and its rates were lost. In other words, the result depended on the real clock.

I changed `AsOfService.storeAsOf` so a parent sheet always comes in as last saved (new query `SheetSnapshotRepository.latestIds`), while the sheet itself is still dated as before. This matches the class's own comment that "a parent is not dated". Two things to know:
- Statements taken as of a date look up parent rates through `RateChain.tiersAsOf`, which still dates them by the parent's own today. Nothing in the test covers that, so I left it alone. It may be worth making the two agree.
- To find the cause I used a temporary debug spec and config under `e2e/`. Both are deleted.
